excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Reactive Power Coordination 
 
Reactive power and voltage control should be coordinated across operating entities. Key points for coordination 
between the generation, transmission, and distribution system, as well as between entities on these systems is 
described in this section. 
 
Transmission to Distribution Coordination 
 
Modeling 
The boundary between TO and DP in power flow , stability analysis, and real-time is usually defined by explicit 
loads modeled as MW and Mvar. These loads may simply be modeled on the high side of the bus/substation or 
potentially modeled behind the step-down transformers and/or equivalent distribution impedances. The voltage 
and reactive power performance of the BES can be impacted by the load power factor (LPF) modeled across the 
TO-DP boundary. Loads should not over-rely on reactive support (lagging or leading) from the BES . Conversely, 
the BES should not solely depend on the load for reactive support (lagging or leading). Coordination between the 
TO and DP is important in determining what the proposed LPF should be at critical load levels (e.g., peak and light 
load).

Reactive Power Coordination 
 
Reactive power and voltage control should be coordinated across operating entities. Key points for coordination 
between the generation, transmission, and distribution system, as well as between entities on these systems is 
described in this section. 
 
Transmission to Distribution Coordination 
 
Modeling 
The boundary between TO and DP in power flow , stability analysis, and real-time is usually defined by explicit 
loads modeled as MW and Mvar. These loads may simply be modeled on the high side of the bus/substation or 
potentially modeled behind the step-down transformers and/or equivalent distribution impedances. The voltage 
and reactive power performance of the BES can be impacted by the load power factor (LPF) modeled across the 
TO-DP boundary. Loads should not over-rely on reactive support (lagging or leading) from the BES . Conversely, 
the BES should not solely depend on the load for reactive support (lagging or leading). Coordination between the 
TO and DP is important in determining what the proposed LPF should be at critical load levels (e.g., peak and light 
load).

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: North American bulk power system; NERC reliability guideline; voluntary guideline. The source limits N-2 to 'some selected' contingencies and ties it to stability limitations and extreme disturbances.

(current lags voltage) and capacitive (current leads voltage) loads and

transfer across a short transmission line can be expressed as 
 
𝑄𝑄𝑟𝑟= 𝑉𝑉𝑟𝑟
𝑋𝑋(𝑉𝑉𝑠𝑠cos 𝛿𝛿− 𝑉𝑉𝑟𝑟) 
 
where Vs and Vr are the sending- and receiving-end voltage magnitudes, respectively, X is the line reactance, a nd 
δ (expressed as φ1- φ2 in Figure 1) is the phase angle difference (“power angle”) between the two ends of the line 
(Figure 1). It is clear from this equation that reactive power is a function of voltage difference, angle difference, 
and electrical impedance; however, angle difference has a relatively small influence while voltage difference and 
impedance are much stronger drivers. For this reason, voltage control is tightly coupled with reactive  power 
control and vice versa.

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

excerpt.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Reactive Power Coordination 
 
Reactive power and voltage control should be coordinated across operating entities. Key points for coordination 
between the generation, transmission, and distribution system, as well as between entities on these systems is 
described in this section. 
 
Transmission to Distribution Coordination 
 
Modeling 
The boundary between TO and DP in power flow , stability analysis, and real-time is usually defined by explicit 
loads modeled as MW and Mvar. These loads may simply be modeled on the high side of the bus/substation or 
potentially modeled behind the step-down transformers and/or equivalent distribution impedances. The voltage 
and reactive power performance of the BES can be impacted by the load power factor (LPF) modeled across the 
TO-DP boundary. Loads should not over-rely on reactive support (lagging or leading) from the BES . Conversely, 
the BES should not solely depend on the load for reactive support (lagging or leading). Coordination between the 
TO and DP is important in determining what the proposed LPF should be at critical load levels (e.g., peak and light 
load).

excerpts.text:
Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

applicability_conditions: NERC Reliability Guideline: Reactive Power Planning (2016); North American bulk power system guidance, voluntary, not a Chinese operating standard.

• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料比较动态与静态无功资源的调节方式、运行方式和电压依赖。

initial_answer.text:
按给定NERC《无功规划》资料：动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化自动、连续地实时调节无功出力，可用于维持设定电压或按电压下垂模式运行；部分电力电子型设备可在电气周波级响应（如STATCOM约50 ms）。

静态无功资源在额定电压下为固定无功出力，其容量随电压平方变化；按系统条件投切，可手动或自动，但接入后即提供固定的额定无功贡献，例如固定并联电容器和电抗器。
assumptions: 仅依据给定的NERC《Reliability Guideline: Reactive Power Planning》摘录；其余检索片段为无关的可靠性评价体系或机构介绍，未用于支撑结论。
missing_information: 所给页面摘录在“Fixed Shunt Devices…is dependent on”处截断，故静态元件电压依赖的完整表述未提取到；也未给出动态资源的具体电压带宽、下垂系数或设备特定响应时间适用范围。

range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices

initial_answer.text:
按给定NERC《无功规划》资料：动态无功资源在指定电压带宽内随电网电压变化自动、连续地实时调节无功出力，可用于维持设定电压或按电压下垂模式运行；部分电力电子型设备可在电气周波级响应（如STATCOM约50 ms）。

静态无功资源在额定电压下为固定无功出力，其容量随电压平方变化；按系统条件投切，可手动或自动，但接入后即提供固定的额定无功贡献，例如固定并联电容器和电抗器。

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: 适用于北美大电力系统；该指南建议为自愿性，区域做法不同。

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料分别说明N-1与选定N-2的要求；无操作员干预这一限定在所给段落中具体绑定哪种工况？

initial_answer.text:
NERC《Reactive Power Planning》指南所述：N-1指失去一个元件（单一故障）后，系统须在无操作员干预下立即保持在紧急热额定值和电压限值内，稳态与稳定要求均适用，且在所有时段（含预测最小、最大负荷）均须具备该能力；选定N-2仅在确定稳定限值时要求系统能承受，并连同更严重但概率更低的极端扰动不致电压崩溃、级联或失稳。

“无操作员干预”在给定段落中绑定于N-1单一故障后的暂态工况，而非N-2或极端扰动。

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料说明短线路无功传输关系用了哪些建模前提、受哪些量影响；不要做数值计算或推广到任意长线路。

initial_answer.text:
NERC资料对短线路无功传输关系的前提是忽略线路电阻R和对地电容B，并采用正弦稳态相量模型；此时Qr≈Vr(cosδ·Vs−Vr)/X。

该式表明无功功率受两端电压幅值差与相角差δ、线路电抗X影响；其中相角影响相对较小，电压差与电抗是更强的驱动因素。

以上仅为短线路近似，不能直接推广到任意长线路；本回答不做数值计算。

and electrical impedance; however, angle difference has a relatively small influence while voltage difference and 
impedance are much stronger drivers. For this reason, voltage control is tightly coupled with reactive  power 
control and vice versa.

initial_answer.text:
NERC资料对短线路无功传输关系的前提是忽略线路电阻R和对地电容B，并采用正弦稳态相量模型；此时Qr≈Vr(cosδ·Vs−Vr)/X。

该式表明无功功率受两端电压幅值差与相角差δ、线路电抗X影响；其中相角影响相对较小，电压差与电抗是更强的驱动因素。

以上仅为短线路近似，不能直接推广到任意长线路；本回答不做数值计算。

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料，正常母线电压是否就能证明电压稳定？解释资料能够支持的判断及故障分析边界。

answer.text:
不能。NERC资料指出：维持所有母线在正常和事故条件下可接受电压需足够无功资源；且系统应在N-1、选定N-2及极端扰动下不发生电压崩溃。因此仅凭正常母线电压不能证明电压稳定。

excerpts.text:
and it is usually necessary to site reactive devices near or at the location 
that is deficient in reactive support. Typically, reactive power supply is provided where it is needed to minimize 
losses. The ability of power system to maintain acceptable voltage at all buses under normal and contingency 
operating conditions requires sufficient reactive resources. 
 
Reactive power resources are generally differentiated between static and dynamic resources  and are usually 
defined by reactive power output controllability once connected to the grid: 
4 NERC Glossary of Terms.  Available:  http://www.nerc.com/files/glossary_of_terms.pdf  
NERC | Reactive Power Planning Guideline  | December 2016  
3

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

applicability_conditions: 北美大电力系统；该指南为自愿性建议，非中国运行标准。

and it is usually necessary to site reactive devices near or at the location 
that is deficient in reactive support. Typically, reactive power supply is provided where it is needed to minimize 
losses. The ability of power system to maintain acceptable voltage at all buses under normal and contingency 
operating conditions requires sufficient reactive resources. 
 
Reactive power resources are generally differentiated between static and dynamic resources  and are usually 
defined by reactive power output controllability once connected to the grid: 
4 NERC Glossary of Terms.  Available:  http://www.nerc.com/files/glossary_of_terms.pdf  
NERC | Reactive Power Planning Guideline  | December 2016  
3

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

and it is usually necessary to site reactive devices near or at the location 
that is deficient in reactive support. Typically, reactive power supply is provided where it is needed to minimize 
losses. The ability of power system to maintain acceptable voltage at all buses under normal and contingency 
operating conditions requires sufficient reactive resources. 
 
Reactive power resources are generally differentiated between static and dynamic resources  and are usually 
defined by reactive power output controllability once connected to the grid: 
4 NERC Glossary of Terms.  Available:  http://www.nerc.com/files/glossary_of_terms.pdf  
NERC | Reactive Power Planning Guideline  | December 2016  
3

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices 
have a fixed nominal rating and their reactive power production or consumption is dependent on

Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料，动态资源的调节特性是否足以确定匿名厂站的补偿容量并保证故障后电压稳定？给出有据解释和具体资料缺口。

initial_answer.text:
否。NERC资料只说明动态无功资源可在指定电压带宽内自动连续调节（如STATCOM约50ms响应），属通用定性描述，未给出该匿名厂站的容量、接线、负荷与电压限值，故不能据此确定补偿容量或保证故障后电压稳定。

要判断，至少需该厂站的电压限值、N-1故障场景及动态资源无功能力数据。

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected. 
 
Static reactive resources generally include the following elements: 
• Fixed Shunt Devices: fixed shunt reactive devices include shunt capacitors and reactors. These devices

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

Background 
 
• Dynamic reactive resources  adjust reactive power output automatically in real-time over a c ontinuous 
range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

actual_question: 按给定NERC资料，动态资源的调节特性是否足以确定匿名厂站的补偿容量并保证故障后电压稳定？给出有据解释和具体资料缺口。

initial_answer.text:
否。NERC资料只说明动态无功资源可在指定电压带宽内自动连续调节（如STATCOM约50ms响应），属通用定性描述，未给出该匿名厂站的容量、接线、负荷与电压限值，故不能据此确定补偿容量或保证故障后电压稳定。

要判断，至少需该厂站的电压限值、N-1故障场景及动态资源无功能力数据。
assumptions: 仅依据所给NERC资料作答，不补充外部数据。
missing_information: 匿名厂站的拓扑、负荷水平、电压限值、N-1/N-2故障定义及动态资源无功容量与模型参数均未给出。
